about.title: Personal Injury Help in Weed, California
about.longDescription: Weed is a small community, but its roads still see their share of collisions. Public records show 2 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 2 people hurt along corridors like S Weed Boulevard, Rt 97, and I-5. Reports tend to cluster on Fridays between noon and 2 p.m., a window when local and through-traffic overlap. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, or in any accident around town, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Weed with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't handle your case ourselves. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Our job is simply to make that first connection easier so you can focus on healing while someone with legal knowledge looks at what happened and explains your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Connect With an Attorney Through LawProactive

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. Claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as 6 months, so it helps to get informed early.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible for the accident — your share of fault simply reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate it.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Truly Lost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in ordinary injury cases, so an attorney can pursue the full extent of what happened to you.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no fee out of pocket to get started.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Weed?
items.answer: California generally allows 2 years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city or county road issue, the deadline to file a notice can be as short as 6 months. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible so you don't lose your window.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to be reported in Weed?
items.answer: Based on public crash records, reported collisions in Weed tend to occur along S Weed Boulevard, Rt 97, and I-5, with reports clustering on Fridays between noon and 2 p.m. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any road's safety.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for what happened. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, so it's still worth exploring your options.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency. That means they only collect a fee if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is not a law firm. We're a free service that connects injured people in Weed and throughout Siskiyou County with independent personal injury attorneys who can evaluate their situation.
